events.summary: Ministry prepared to provide five mammography machines to major cancer-treatment hospitals.
National Hospital’s Institute of Neurology was renovated at a cost of Rs. 99 million.
Health Ministry allocated Rs. 52 million to modernise the two neurology wards.
Construction of the Rambukkana–Galagedara section is scheduled to begin.
IOM concluded cash assistance for more than 4,000 cyclone-affected families across seven districts.
The ministry scheduled government nursing appointments for 515 graduates.
The IMF Executive Board approved the fifth and sixth combined reviews of Sri Lanka’s EFF.
Main structure for 112 Mahargama housing units was completed.
State Vesak celebrations and nationwide religious, social and environmental activities are scheduled to begin.
Cabinet approved selling part of state paddy stocks to raise funds and storage for the next Yala purchase.
India handed over 134 donated pickup vehicles for the Sri Lanka Police.
Five forests and the Kuda Bubula spring are planned for designation as protected reserves.
A joint Forest Conservation Unit was established to protect forests from deforestation.
Twelve colposcopy machines were installed in government hospitals.
Funding was set aside for six additional colposcopy machines.
Construction began on Ampara's multipurpose town hall.
Funding was provided for Ampara District infrastructure works in 2026.
The government plans 2 trillion rupees in capital expenditure for 2027.
Police announced implementation of a special Vesak security plan.
Officials discussed permanent appointments for 517 nursing graduates.
Structured interviews began for 1,989 health service assistant vacancies.
Government fuel and electricity restrictions were relaxed for Vesak celebrations.
The 2026 budget allocated compensation for crop losses linked to Nilwala salt barrier flooding.
Reported 2025 maintenance expenditure across Sri Lanka's expressways.
WHO designated Angoda's NIID as a joint international dengue research and training centre.
Police called for applications to recruit 50 women sub-inspectors and 2,600 women constables.
National QR payments promotion programme launched to encourage cashless transactions.
Monthly daycare allowance proposed for eligible children of overseas workers.
Initial funding of Rs. 10 million set aside for the daycare allowance.
Cabinet decided against a water tariff revision during the first half of 2026.
Government insurance compensation planned up to Rs. 100,000 per hectare for damaged crops.
Ministry signed an agreement to procure 104 buses for Lanka Metro Transit.
District committee approved a pilot dog census and vaccination programme in three divisional secretariats.
Central Bank introduced an online complaint management system for financial consumers.
Health authorities unveiled nationwide maternal screening for HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B.
A further 500 million rupees was allocated in 2024 despite construction being suspended.
The estimated cost of the auditorium project was 3,154.88 million rupees.
The contractor had been paid 195.14 million rupees for completed work.
Auditor report said construction had been suspended for more than five years.
A contract was awarded to restore several landslide sites between Nanu Oya and Ambewela.
Financial compensation was awarded to 1,898 CEB employees taking voluntary retirement.
Conservation works and visitor facilities are planned to develop Yapahuwa as a tourism destination.
Government bears Rs. 100 per litre of diesel to keep the retail price at Rs. 392.
ADB-backed installation of seven cardiac catheterisation laboratories at Colombo, Kandy and Jaffna hospitals.
JICA-supported installation of six cardiac catheterisation laboratories at five hospitals.
Cabinet approved awards for seven locally funded expressway construction packages.
Yal Devi train service resumes between Colombo Fort and Kankesanthurai.
Cabinet approved appointing MPs as district health coordination officers nationwide.
Sri Lanka Foundation returned unused salary-budget funds to the Treasury.
Management board approved returning unused funds to the Treasury.
Aswesuma spent Rs. 148.4 billion supporting two million beneficiary families in 2025.
Vietnam formally donated 100 metric tons of fertiliser to Sri Lanka.
Cabinet approved the university digital transformation project at an estimated cost of Rs. 476 million.
Cabinet approved land acquisition for development of the Kelani Valley Railway.
Public consultation begins on proposed electricity tariff revisions for the second and third quarters.
Government introduced online advance seat booking for long-distance passengers as a pilot.
Government allocated relief funding for people affected by the Middle East conflict.
